The Cua Driver binary (trycua/cua) — the background computer-use driver that
drives a desktop's apps via the AT-SPI accessibility tree and input, with
window enumeration and screenshots. Installs the pinned release archive into
/opt/cua-driver (the binary's aux files resolve relative to its real path, so
they stay together) and symlinks /usr/local/bin/cua-driver into it, plus the
runtime libraries the binary links against (libxi, glibc, libxkbcommon) and the
AT-SPI bus. The driver runs as a desktop-session daemon; the `cua-session`
candy wires that. Verifiable on the built image: the binary and its aux files
are present and `cua-driver --version` prints a version.

## Acceptance plan

This candy's `plan:` — the runnable spec `charly check` executes against a live deployment. `check:` steps are idempotent probes; `run:` steps change state.

| Intent | Step |
|---|---|
| `run` | install the pinned Cua Driver release into /opt/cua-driver (binary + aux files together — the driver resolves aux files relative to its real path) |
| `run` | symlink the driver and its cursor-theme compiler onto PATH |
| `run` | disable Cua Driver's default-on content-free telemetry (an unattended CI image should not phone home; the operator can re-enable it) |
| `check` | the Cua Driver binary and its aux files are installed together |
| `check` | the driver resolves its aux files and prints a version (proves the real-path aux resolution works through the symlink) |
